Even in destinations that are overall very safe, petty theft is a risk. For instance, many European cities are pickpocketing hotspots, and crowded tourist attractions like Christmas markets make ideal hunting grounds for thieves.

Thankfully, there are steps you can take to protect yourself. I’ve gathered real-life anecdotes from my fellow travelers at TPG so you know what to look for, and our top tips to help you protect yourself.

The first and easiest precaution you can take is to minimize your loss if you do get robbed.

That means leaving your flashy jewelry or designer-brand luggage at home, as these can often attract thieves. And be sure to make copies of crucial documents and store them in a safe digital place, where you can easily access them if your hard copies get lost.

What about travel insurance? Some policies may cover theft, so check the coverage offered by your credit card. You may want to consider buying additional coverage for particularly costly items.

This one can be tricky, but do your best not to advertise your status as a tourist. In Europe, for instance, dressing in neutral clothing can help you blend in with the locals (meanwhile, bright colors and American sports apparel scream “foreigner”).

Check a map and figure out where you’re going before leaving your hotel to avoid wandering around looking clueless. Familiarize yourself with your destination’s public transport system; thieves often prowl transportation hubs in search of tourists who are out of their element.

The more distracted you are, the easier it is to get separated you from your valuables. Instead of getting absorbed in your phone, keep your gaze up and walk with purpose. Plus, this will help you soak in your surroundings and make the most of your trip.

Public transportation is a pickpocket’s playground, especially lines that cover tourist draws like Rome’s notorious 64 bus and Lisbon’s iconic yellow Tram 28.

Senior editor Lyndsey Matthews says, “When I was 11, I was in London and saw two teens try to pickpocket my grandma on the way out of the Tube.” Thankfully, all they got was some dirty tissues and seashells.

Keep your bags close and in sight while riding public transport. If you’re carrying a daypack, turn it around and carry it on your chest with the straps looped around your shoulders. Be particularly cautious at train, tram and subway stops, where thieves can dash on, grab your suitcase and bolt before the doors shut again.

Thieves often work together, with one creating a spectacle or disturbance — a spilled drink, an argument, a stumble on the metro — while the other preys on distracted bystanders.

Senior editor Colin Hogan once lost his wallet to a pickpocket in Montreal: “She was working alongside a street performer, and as the performer would gather people into a circle around him to view the performance, she would come behind and steal things from bags or pockets while they were distracted.”

If something happens, resist the urge to stare. Stay focused on yourself and your belongings instead.

You’ve probably heard not to leave your wallet in your back pocket, where it will be easy pickings. But skilled thieves can navigate front pockets with ease, or snatch purses and disappear into the crowd before you can blink.

Lead writer Katie Genter has a relative who got robbed on public transportation in Paris: “She was carrying one of those huge purse bags without a zipper on top,” she says, which would be child’s play for most pickpockets.

To reduce your risk, stick to bags that zip closed, and consider clipping the zippers together for an added layer of protection. Opt for a crossbody bag or fanny pack, which is harder to snatch than a shoulder bag, or a money belt you can keep under your clothes.

As travelers have gotten smarter, so have criminals.

One popular tactic is to slice through the strap of a crossbody bag, then make off with it. Director of content strategy Carly Helfand says, “I’ve had my bag sliced from the bottom on the Prague metro and the phone stolen out of it!”

Consider investing in a theft-resistant bag made of tougher material that’s harder for thieves to cut into. I’m a big fan of this one, which also has locking zippers, a cut-resistant strap and RFID-blocking credit card slots.

Remember, you don’t need to make your bag impenetrable. Simply making it harder to access is often enough to convince opportunistic thieves to move on in search of easier targets.

It goes without saying to not leave anything valuable at your seat while you run to the restroom or grab napkins from the bar. But thieves may be bold enough to snatch items from right in front of you, or even out of your hands.

Director of UX Research Mindy Pastrovich says that in Cape Town, “my friend was talking to a guy who asked for her number, and when she took out her phone to give it to him, he stole it and ran away.”

Stay aware of your surroundings. Keep a firm grip on your phone or camera when you’re using it (a wrist strap or lanyard can help), and tuck them out of sight when you’re not. If you sit down in any public place, like a hotel lobby or train car, loop your bag strap around your chair leg or clip your suitcase to the luggage rack.

It can be tempting to keep all your valuables on your person, where you can keep track of them constantly. But even the most vigilant travelers can fall prey to clever thieves.

TPG assistant marketing manager Paige Stepanian has a friend who got pickpocketed on the Barcelona metro. “She had her phone in a fanny pack that was at the front of her, facing into a group of friends. It happened so fast, by the time we realized her phone was gone the person who took it was already off the train!”

In fact, your items are generally safer in your hotel room than your day pack. Keep what you need in a money belt or theft-resistant crossbody purse, and leave the rest in your room. It’s always a good idea to leave valuables out of sight, or better yet, lock them in the hotel safe or your suitcase.

Scams and confidence games can take unexpected forms. I recently heard of a couple friends of a friend who, while stopped in an airport, were approached by a man offering to give them directions. Meanwhile, his accomplice was walking off with the travelers’ luggage.

Other scams may involve someone putting jewelry or accessories on you without your permission or handing you a drink you didn’t ask for — then demanding payment later. Be wary of anyone who is overly friendly, and set boundaries politely but firmly.

On a recent trip to Zanzibar, I couldn’t even take a casual stroll on the beach without at least one person trying to give me a tide pool tour — which I’m sure he would have charged handsomely for, had I not resolutely walked off and left him in the shallows.

If you’re traveling by car, never leave valuables in view when you park, even if you think you’ll be right back.

My friend once had her purse stolen from a rental car in Hawaii while she was stopped at a scenic overlook for a quick photo. Not only did she lose all her money, she also had a heck of a time getting home without an ID.

In areas where break-ins are common, it’s a good idea to empty the car and leave the doors unlocked any time you leave. That way, if a thief decides to take a look inside, you won’t have to deal with the cost and headache of repairing a broken window.

When senior content strategist Gabrielle Bernardini was in Cabo, Mexico, a gas station attendant asked her for her credit card. “I gave it to him, and he handed it to someone next to him, who then ran into the convenience store. Next, I got an alert from Amex that about $4,000 was charged to my card.”

Thankfully, she contacted Amex right away and was able to get the fraudulent charge wiped in about a week.

Despite all the horror stories I’ve mentioned, theft is still relatively uncommon. I’ve been to Europe more times than I can count and never had anything stolen (knock on wood).

Following the tips above won’t guarantee you don’t fall victim to petty theft, but it will significantly slash your risk.

#6034. Considering The Bilt Palladium Card? Here’s Why You Should Apply Soon…

The Bilt Palladium Card (learn more) is the most premium card in the Bilt credit card portfolio, and personally, it’s one of my all-around favorite cards (Rates & Fees). If you’ve been on the fence about picking up this very lucrative card, I’d highly recommend applying ASAP, and definitely before the end of 2026. Let me explain…

The Bilt Palladium Card is one of my favorite credit cards, and it’s the card that gets the most of my spending. Just to cover some of the very basics, the card has a $495 annual fee (Rates & Fees), and offers the following value proposition at the moment:

For me, the logic of picking up this card is pretty straightforward, and I’ve shared that in much more detail. The idea is that the combination of the 2x points plus 4% back in the form of Bilt Cash is an unrivaled return on spending, especially given the value of Bilt points. Spending on Bilt cards also earns you Bilt elite status, and that unlocks better Rent Day promotions.

On the most basic level, that Bilt Cash earns me 1x points per dollar spent on my housing payments (without any sort of fee), plus I take advantage of the Points Accelerator feature, which earns me an extra 1x points per dollar spent up to five times per year, by redeeming $200 in Bilt Cash. In other words, this card earns me 3x points on up to $25,000 of spending per year, plus I’m being rewarded on my housing spending.

Points with Bilt rack up really quickly, so if you spend quite a bit on credit cards, I do think this is tough to beat. And this doesn’t even account for the value of the hotel credit, as you can stack the credit card’s hotel credit with some Bilt Cash to get an even bigger discount on a hotel stay.

As I’ve covered, changes are coming to Bilt as of 2027. While the changes are being made in the name of “simplifying” things, I’d argue that it only creates even more complexity, at least for existing members. Essentially, starting in 2027, Bilt members will earn points for their housing payment as a percentage of their card spending, in lieu of earning 4% back in Bilt Cash on all their spending.

The good news is that through December 31, 2026, you can still opt into the old system for being rewarded, and that will then be honored in 2027 and beyond. This applies both to existing cardmembers, and those who pick up the card before then, and select this as their earnings preference.

The idea is that if you opt into this grandfathered system and have the Bilt Palladium Card:

Just as an example, I have more Bilt Cash than I can redeem (at least as someone who is scared of helicopters, and who finds Blacklane to be overpriced even with the Bilt Cash redemption options). However, the Bilt Cash I earn gets me 1x points on all my housing payments, maxed out Points Accelerator redemptions, elevated Rent Day offers, and Lyft and Walgreens redemptions, so I get $120 in credit with each business per year.

I think the Bilt Palladium can still absolutely be worth it under the new system, where you’d be rewarded on housing payments per the below, and would also earn $600 in Bilt Cash annually (starting in 2027), but without the 4% back in the form of Bilt Cash on spending.

So if the Bilt Palladium Card has at all been on your radar, this would definitely be the time to apply. After all, this is what will allow you to maximize value on the card in the long run.

Bilt is making some program changes as of 2027, which are a mixed bag. From my perspective, the biggest loss is that cardmembers are by default being switched from a system where they earn points plus flexible Bilt Cash for their spending, to one where they earn points plus rewards at a certain rate toward housing payments.

At least for me, the old system is definitely better, and the good news is that through the end of 2026, you can continue to opt into the old system of earning points plus Bilt Cash for spending, and then that will be honored in 2027 and beyond. This applies not just to those who already have the card, but also those who open the card before the end of the year. So if the Bilt Palladium Card has been on your radar, I’d recommend applying in the near future.

#6033. 6 Airlines With 40-Inch Premium Economy Seat Pitch

Although some airlines, like Air New Zealand, offer more, 40 inches (102 cm) is the golden number for seat pitch in premium economy. Any more is meaningless for all but the tallest of passengers. It represents a significant step up from the 30 to 32 inches (76 to 81 cm) that you can usually expect in economy class.

Seat engineers can use this space to produce deep recline and leg and calf rests for a supremely comfortable seat without passengers needing to pay for lie-flat business class. The additional space also makes it possible for passengers to be productive throughout cruise on their laptop or tablet. Examples of airlines that offer 40 inches of seat pitch in premium economy include All Nippon Airways, Cathay Pacific, Emirates, and ITA Airways.

Not all airlines offer 40 inches of seat pitch in their premium economy cabins because it takes effort, along with a reduction in the overall number of seats that can be sold. For its 787-9, ANA took the plunge and increased seat pitch by two inches (five cm). ANA also grew the recline range by the same amount, achieving a total of nine inches (23 cm) of recline. These seats are available on ANA's 206-seat 787-9s and not on its 246 and 215-seat Dreamliners.

The table below shows the number of seats available in each class of these three Dreamliner configurations for ANA. It shows what ANA has sacrificed for the additional two inches of premium economy pitch, which is nine economy class seats:

Another airline that has gone to great lengths to give its premium passengers access to 40 inches of pitch is Cathay Pacific, although it insists that its premium economy is more than just extra legroom. The carrier has retrofitted some of its aging 777-300ERs to bring in this capability. “For our Boeing 777-300ER, we have a very clear goal, which is to design Premium Economy as a cabin that thrives on its own merits – a product that reflects the customer’s needs and the premium differentiation,” says Vivian Lo, General Manager, Customer Experience & Design at Cathay Pacific.

All premium economy seats on Cathay Pacific's A350s also give passengers 40 inches of pitch. The room is matched by a full-length leg rest and an adjustable armrest. You can access a near business class level of customizability in these seats. Cathay Pacific's business class is also known for the "raft of useful features" incorporated within it. Examples include a dimmable reading light, slide-out coffee table, and a petite amenities storage space.

Flying on the world's largest commercial aircraft, Emirates' premium economy gives passengers access to 40 inches of pitch and 19.5 inches (49.3 cm) of width. Eight inches of recline provides additional comfort. This product was unveiled in 2020. Sir Tim Clark, Emirates president, said: “The Emirates A380 is already one of the most sought-after travel experiences in the skies, and now we’ve made it even better. While others cut back, Emirates is working hard to restore the products and services that we’ve had to suspend or adjust."

The table below shows the various seating configurations for Emirates A380s, allowing you to understand the number of 40-inch premium economy seats available in each case. It uses data collected by Simple Flying and shows that premium economy is available aboard a surprisingly small number of Emirates A380 configurations:

ITA Airways has premium economy products on its A321neo, A330-200, A330-900, and A350-900. The A330-200 and A350-900 are older aircraft with less space in premium economy. The carrier's A321neo and A330neo offer the best products, giving passengers access to a spacious 40 inches of pitch. Both jets are equipped with Safran seats, with the A330neo using the Z535i and the A321neo deploying the Z600. These products are relatively similar, but with minor alterations made to make them compatible with widebody and narrowbody planes, respectively.

As with any great premium economy product, there is much more to ITA's premium economy than space. You'll find a generous touchscreen measuring 15.6 inches (39.6 cm), along with power ports, a coat hook, a legrest, and a footrest. You'll also be able to enjoy food inspired by Italy's legendary cuisine, as pictured above.

The Italian carrier's premium product has been well-received by trip reviewers. Upgraded Points traveled on an ITA A330neo and wrote: "The service from the flight attendants didn’t rise to the wow factor, but it was good. The hard product on the flight was superior to the soft product, and I would definitely fly ITA Airways again. The cabin interior looked amazing, everything felt new and clean."

The table below uses Planespotters.net data to show Qantas' current widebody fleet, revealing how we can expect the incoming A350-1000ULR to fit into it.

The comfort available onboard Project Sunrise flights will extend beyond the premium economy seat. Qantas will dedicate space to a wellbeing zone. Both premium economy and economy passengers can use this space for hydration and self-serve refreshments, along with spaces for stretching and guided movement. Although this area is essential for economy passengers who would otherwise spend over 20 hours in a cramped seat, it will also provide fantastic comfort and variety for premium economy passengers.

Premium economy has grown significantly in popularity over the past decade.

Premium economy onboard Starlux's A350-900s can be found over the aircraft's wings front section, right behind the second door. It includes 36 seats in a 2-4-2 configuration, while row 24 has just two outer pairs of seats. These seats, which are RECARO PL3530, all have 40 inches of seat pitch. They also have a width of 18.7 inches (47.5 cm), which is a small but noticeable step up from the 18 inches (45.7 cm) you can expect in standard economy.

Sleep and entertainment are the priority for the airline's product. All passengers can enjoy bedding from the Taiwanese brand Sleepy Tofu. This includes a luxury pillow with a quilted design. Entertainment comes from the 15.6-inch (39.6 cm) high-definition entertainment screen on the back of every seat. These screens are loaded with countless TV shows, music, movies, and games, and come with noise-canceling headphones so you aren't disturbed by the surrounding passengers.

Finally, premium economy passengers are given amenity kits from SMILEY Company. These kits are co-branded with Starlux Airlines and include socks, an eye mask, lip balm, and hand lotion. Please note that the kit is only available on routes to North America.

Starlux's marketing of this product focuses as much on the vibe that has been created in the cabin as the hard product. "Passengers are welcomed with warm and uplifting feel. The subtle color combinations of warm brown and gray tones are at the same time calming and comforting but also expressive, creating a very specific atmosphere of relaxed elegance to the whole premium economy cabin," Starlux writes.

#6031. Latino Democrats celebrate midterm gains, with warning for party

California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez, here at a 2020 news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center, is the chair of BOLD PAC. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

Latino voters moved sharply away from Republicans this year, and a record number of Latino Democratic candidates were elected.

But California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez has a warning for her fellow Democrats.

“Latino voters gave Democrats a two-year lease, but it expires in 2028 unless the party changes its playbook for good,” said Sánchez, who leads the campaign arm of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

Failure to address rising costs and push back against President Donald Trump’s immigration agenda could once again scramble the political calculus and spark another realignment in two years, said House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar of California.

“While Latinos shifted towards Democrats and … gave us this mandate as a party, Democrats must continue to earn their trust, not just every two years, but every single day,’’ he said.

Leaders of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus joined newly elected Latino members on Tuesday for a news conference to celebrate the recent wins and the role the group played in securing the House majority for Democrats. The caucus will boast 55 members in the next Congress, its largest roster ever, according to Sánchez.

BOLD PAC, the caucus’ campaign arm, invested heavily in Latino candidates this year, including in primaries.

California Rep. Salud Carbajal noted that BOLD PAC raised more than $18.5 million this cycle, which helped candidates leverage outside money.

Working-class majority-Latino districts in South Texas, Arizona and California were among the areas that provided Democrats with their biggest wins. Democrats capitalized on voter dissatisfaction over rising costs, the very issue that helped Trump and the GOP make significant gains among Hispanic voters just two years earlier.

But the wins weren’t limited to districts with sizable Latino populations.

Rep.-elect Denise Powell, who flipped a swing seat in Nebraska, credited BOLD PAC for playing a key role in her win.

“Yes, there are Latinos in Omaha, and those Latinos actually helped decide this race,’’ she said. “BOLD believed in me as a candidate, but they also believed in our community.”

Rep.-elect Bobby Pulido, who came to politics after a successful career as a Latin Grammy-winning Tejano singer, flipped a redrawn South Texas border district that Trump would have carried by 18 points in 2024.

“A lot of people feel like they don't belong to either party. But there's one thing about Latinos is we belong to each other,’’ Pulido said. “It's very hard to be a Latino right now in this country. … I expect to see us united, more united than ever, because it's a tough time right now.”

Several of the winning candidates deployed novel strategies to reach voters. Pulido famously began performing at quinceañeras after his Republican opponent dismissed him as a performer.

Colorado Rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, who flipped a battleground district north of Denver, attended World Cup and Broncos watch parties. “If people don't hear our message, then it doesn't matter,’’ he said.

The candidates “met those voters where they were,’’ Sánchez said. “They went into those communities and interacted in a very real and meaningful way. That's something I think that strategists or consultants don't always get. It's not just about pumping out lots of television commercials.”

Amid those successes for Latino Democrats, Florida, home to one of the largest Latino electorates in the country, was a different story. Republicans held all three majority-Latino districts in the Sunshine State, though former news anchor Eliott Rodriguez, the son of Cuban immigrants, came within half a percentage point of unseating GOP Rep. María Elvira Salazar in a district that backed Trump by 15 points in 2024.

BOLD PAC did have a victory to celebrate in Florida, with Rep. Darren Soto, the deputy chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, narrowly prevailing in a district that Republicans redrew as one that no longer had a Latino majority.

“The redistricting wars ended up failing because of the investment by BOLD PAC,’’ Soto said.

#6030. Influencer Uses AI To Score American First Class Upgrade… And Overpays

There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.

People are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that. Can AI help you find award flights and secure upgrades? It’s something I’d like to study in a bit more detail and write about in the coming weeks, but I just saw a post on Instagram that piqued my interest, so I figured it would make for a fun story. Consider this just a little teaser, for the time being.

An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface. The idea is simply that ChatGPT helped someone secure an upgrade through the standard means — it’s not like ChatGPT used his/her/their charm to sweet talk someone into an upgrade by dressing up nicely. 😉

Let me actually just quote the description of the video, which covers most of the content:

What happens when you ask ChatGPT to upgrade your flight to first class?

I tried this on my flight in two weeks and it actually worked.

Go to ChatGPT and switch from Chat to Work at the top. Start a new chat and give it your airline and confirmation code.

Prompt 1:“Ask me every question you need about my credit cards, my miles, and my memberships, and map out every upgrade currency I own for this exact flight.”

ChatGPT shows you that you’ve been sitting on upgrade power this whole time without even knowing it.

Prompt 2:“Now look up my exact flight, check how empty the first class cabin is, and tell me every way I can get up there, ranked from free to cheapest.”

Prompt 3:“Now go get me the upgrade. Use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.”

ChatGPT opens its own browser, logs into your airline, and actually chases that seat for you while you sit back and do nothing.

You can watch the video for yourself below.

A post shared by Maverick Maltin | AI & ChatGPT (@mavgpt)

I don’t want to suggest AI isn’t useful, but I’d say that the example given is actually very poor. First of all, let’s be clear about what’s actually going on here. He had booked a business class ticket on American from Los Angeles (LAX) to London (LHR), and then upgraded to first class.

Now, in the first place, something isn’t fully accurate here:

Okay, maybe he edited the dates, or something, which is fine, and it’s besides the point, but as a detail oriented airline nerd, I couldn’t help but notice those things. Anyway, let’s assume this is all accurate:

To me, this is kind of where AI falls flat, and it isn’t the correct way to use it. The prompt was reportedly to “use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.” This is where I get confused — you’d think that AI would be able to scour reviews online, and see that American first class isn’t (well, or wasn’t) really viewed as a product that’s worth the premium.

If AI were really providing useful advice here, it would’ve recommend waitlisting with the systemwide upgrade, and otherwise recommending the guy save his 70,000 miles, and use them for something else. While there are definitely some strong use cases for AI, I think this is actually a pretty poor showing of what it can do.

By the way, keep in mind that under United’s updated contract of carriage, using AI to help service reservations is banned, and could potentially get your ticket canceled. Whether there’s any enforcement of that remains to be seen.

While the thought of using AI to score an upgrade might sound great, don’t count on it actually getting you the best deal. An AI whiz claims he has the secret to using AI to upgrade to first class. All AI did was use the instant upgrade offer that was available directly on American’s website, and it didn’t even encourage him to skip the upgrade due to it not being worthwhile, or waitlisting the upgrade with a systemwide upgrade, which is objectively a much better deal than 70,000 miles.

What do you make of this AI “assistance” for a first class upgrade?

#6028. Delta Air Lines Drops 9 Routes From Major Hub: See Full List Now

Delta Air Lines has nine hubs across the US. They include New York JFK, from which OAG data shows the carrier has 194 departures per day in November 2026. It is the carrier's sixth-busiest hub in this sense. However, widebody aircraft means it jumps to fifth for seats for sale. Widebodies and long-haul activity sees it become the second-busiest hub for available seat miles.

Like all airlines, Delta is not immune to route churn. Between May 2026 and January 2027, the SkyTeam member has removed — or will end — nine routes from its JFK network, most of which are domestic. Some existed for decades.

All have already ceased or will do so soon, with no flights scheduled beyond the stated end months. The list excludes very time-limited operations for special events, such as flights from JFK to New Mexico for the Albuquerque International Balloon Festival, which is held in October. The temporary route, which has been served since 2024, is likely to return in 2027.

Flown By Another Carrier From JFK In 2027?

1997-2000, 2008-2011, 2019-2020, 2025-2026

Yes: JetBlue. United may begin flights if it returns to JFK next year

Republic E175, very occasionally Endeavor CRJ900

2009-2012, 2025-2026 (inherited from Northwest Airlines)

At 2,066 nautical miles (3,826 km) each way, the transcontinental link to Palm Springs was Delta's longest scheduled A319 service in 2026. In fact, the equipment has not covered more distance since 2021, when Delta ceased using the small narrowbody between Boston and Seattle. JFK-Palm Springs was the airline's third-longest A319 route in the past 20 years, with Philadelphia-Los Angeles briefly seeing the type in 2011.

The following list only includes international links that Delta pulled in or since May 2026. As such, the carrier's service from JFK to Brussels, which ended in January this year, is excluded. That route was inaugurated in 1991 using the Airbus A310, although the Boeing 767 was deployed for years until the final service.

Flown By Another Carrier From JFK In 2027?

Yes: American (JetBlue pulled out in September 2026)

Yes: JetBlue and American (the latter carrier pulls out on January 4, 2027)

All airlines from JFK to Bermuda did not do well in the 12 months to August 2026. According to the US Department of Transportation (DOT), they each had a load factor of between 70.3% (JetBlue) and 72.0% (American). Of course, this is only one performance measure, and should not be considered in isolation.

After pulling out of JFK, Delta has shifted to serving the British Overseas Territory in the North Atlantic from New York LaGuardia instead. It'll be hoping for fare and yield advantages from doing so, not least because it is the sole operator, after BermudAir pulled out in July 2026. Time will tell how it does.

The US will have 44% fewer flights next Thursday, leading to lots of temporary changes. Find out more inside!

Northwest began this route from JFK to the airline's then-hub of Memphis in 2009. Until then, that carrier's flights from Greater NYC had existed from Newark and LaGuardia. Delta took over all three routes, although flights from Newark ended in 2012, shortly before the Memphis hub closed. Despite the cessation of service from JFK in June 2026, flights from LaGuardia continue today.

Between September 2025 and August 2026, US DOT data shows that Delta carried 15,091 passengers to/from JFK and, as mentioned earlier, filled barely two-thirds of the available seats. JFK had the airline's second-lowest load factor to Memphis, after Boston (59.4%).

JFK had the second-worst distance-adjusted total revenue per available seat mile figure involving the Tennessee city, and it was even lower than Boston. That's despite 68.9% of JFK passengers only flying to/from the Big Apple, with local traffic being higher-yielding than those connecting elsewhere.

Becoming a savvy award traveler requires mastering two skills: earning points and miles, and redeeming them effectively.

By taking advantage of the best travel rewards credit cards, you can master the first skill. However, the second can be more challenging.

At TPG, we help you redeem transferable points at the maximum value. However, some travelers frequently run into issues finding the award availability they need.

There isn’t a general rule you can follow to make searching for award space easier. Each airline and award search engine has pros, cons and quirks to understand.

Fortunately, you don't need to search every airline's website individually. Several innovative third-party tools can now do much of the hard work for you. Knowing which airline programs to search can also save you time and points.

These are the best ways to find award availability for points and miles across major airlines.

Related: Special offers on TPG's favorite travel tools and services

Several apps and websites let you search across multiple airlines, alliances and programs at once, rather than worrying about the best loyalty program to sift through. Two of our favorites at TPG are: Seats.aero and Point.me.

Seats.aero currently searches more than 20 airline loyalty programs, including major programs like American Airlines AAdvantage, Delta SkyMiles and United MileagePlus. This powerful tool lets you search all these programs simultaneously across multiple routes, dates, classes and transfer partners in seconds. You can also search individual programs across an extended date range to identify available award seats. There are even handy filters so you can limit factors such as the maximum number of points or surcharges.

The platform has also developed several innovative tools to help you find those harder-to-book seats, such as Lufthansa first class, Delta One, All Nippon Airways first class and Qatar Airways Qsuite. You can set alerts across multiple routes, dates, programs and carriers to be notified by text or email if a seat you seek becomes available. There's also an AI Assistant if you don't know where to start.

Point.me searches more than 150 airlines across over 30 loyalty programs, generally checking one departure date at a time. That's particularly useful when you're trying to compare all the ways to book a specific flight, especially through programs Seats.aero doesn't fully support, such as British Airways Club, Iberia Club and Aer Lingus AerClub.

Unlike Seats.aero's cached results, Point.me uses live award searches. It also shows which transferable credit card currencies you can use, highlights applicable transfer bonuses and provides step-by-step instructions for transferring points and completing the booking.

Be aware that neither tool can actually book the ticket for you, so it's still worth confirming the award directly with your chosen airline program before moving any of your valuable transferable points.

Related: These apps and websites make award redemptions easier to find

The major North American airlines have reasonably comprehensive award search engines, so starting with the airline you want to fly is often the simplest option.

However, you'll sometimes find better value through a partner program. Here are some useful places to search.

It's worth comparing prices before booking. American, Delta and United all use dynamic pricing, so the number of miles required for a flight can change considerably depending on the date and demand.

Booking through a partner might save you thousands of points or miles, but don't assume that partner pricing is always fixed.

For example, Aeroplan now uses variable pricing for United-operated awards, so booking the same flight through Air Canada won't necessarily be cheaper than booking directly with United.

European loyalty programs can offer great redemption deals, whether you are taking, say, a business-class flight to Europe for just 40,500 credit card points or an economy flight to London for just 6,000 points.

Here is how to search for the best award availability:

Some of the most aspirational first-class airline products, such as Etihad's A380 Apartments and Emirates' A380 suites, are offered by Middle Eastern airlines.

Here's how to search for award availability.

Emirates first-class awards now come with additional restrictions. Emirates Skywards only allows Silver, Gold and Platinum members to book first-class Classic Rewards. Qantas Frequent Flyer restricts them to Silver members and above, while Aeroplan requires members to hold Aeroplan 35K status or higher to redeem points for Emirates first class.

Related: Emirates first class still wows: Fully enclosed suites and unlimited caviar

Now that you know where to search for award space for your next trip, here are a few tricks to make the process easier.

This is an odd quirk of most award search engines, but you’ll often get different results if you search for your complete itinerary instead of one flight at a time.

If your complete itinerary isn't showing any award availability, try searching for each flight separately. This can help identify which segment is causing the problem, although finding each flight individually doesn't guarantee that the airline can combine them into a single award. The complete journey still needs to meet the program's routing and ticketing rules.

Sometimes, airlines will offer more seats for indirect itineraries than nonstop ones. Why? Airlines believe passengers will pay more for direct fares with cash (compared to indirect ones), so with less demand for connecting itineraries, they may offer additional seats.

Using this married-segment logic in your next search, you may be able to find long-haul, premium-cabin seats you did not think existed. Consider widening your search to connect in another city using a catch-all external tool like Seats.aero.

You might be surprised by the additional availability if you are willing to fly a little farther than your original destination.

However, don't assume you can remove a connecting segment and keep the same award price or availability.

One particularly frustrating issue when booking partner awards is phantom availability. This happens when an airline or search tool displays an award seat that can't actually be booked.

Unfortunately, this remains a problem across several major loyalty programs.

Before transferring points, select the exact flight and proceed as far as possible through the booking process. For an especially valuable redemption requiring a large points transfer, consider contacting the airline to confirm availability first.

Related: Phantom award space: What it is and how to avoid it

Many airline customer service agents are good at their jobs, but you’ll get much better results when you do the work yourself.

Before you call to book an award flight, you should have the exact dates and flight numbers you want. Make your specific requests known early in the conversation.

As soon as you tell the agent where you’re trying to go, say something like, “I have the flight numbers here whenever you’re ready for them.” This way, they don’t waste any time trying to search on their end.

If you’ve done your homework to ensure that there is award space and your routing is valid, these calls will go much more easily.

Ask the agent to confirm the complete itinerary, the number of points or miles required, and the applicable taxes and fees. Once booked, check that the reservation has been ticketed and that every flight is confirmed in the cabin you wanted.

Learning how to find and book award flights is one of the hardest things about award travel — especially when booking premium-cabin seats on a long flight.

Fortunately, tools like Seats.aero and Point.me make it much easier to compare loyalty programs and identify flights that might otherwise take hours to find. Both platforms offer free features, while paid subscriptions unlock more comprehensive searches and other useful tools that can be well worth the cost when hunting for a hard-to-find, long-haul premium-cabin award seat.

If you have a specific airline you wish to fly, use the tables above to search for award space and compare prices across programs before transferring any credit card points and booking your trip.

#6023. Citi AAdvantage Business Card Bonus: 75K Miles Welcome Offer (Double Dip Loyalty Points!)

The Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® is American’s primary co-branded business credit card. We’re currently seeing an excellent limited time welcome offer, which is in line with the highest ever offer that we’ve seen on the card.

That makes this the ideal time to apply for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. Not only that, but this is a card that many people will want, given that it’s my favorite American card for earning AAdvantage elite status, since you can basically double dip Loyalty Points.

Link: Learn more about the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard®

The Citi AAdvantage Business Card currently has a limited time welcome offer of 75,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $5,000 within the first five months. This is a highest-ever offer, in line with the best bonuses I recall seeing on the card (I covered the card’s offer history below). We don’t know when this offer will be pulled.

Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I value AAdvantage miles at 1.5 cents each, so to me the bonus is worth $1,125. There are some incredible uses of American AAdvantage miles, including for travel on some world class partner airlines.

Just to give a few examples of AAdvantage mileage redemptions, you could redeem 57,500 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Finnair business class award from Dallas (DFW) to Helsinki (HEL)…

…or you could redeem 60,000 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Japan Airlines business class award from Dallas (DFW) to Tokyo (HND)…

…or you could redeem 40,000 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Etihad business class award (or 50,000 miles for an Etihad first class award) from Abu Dhabi (AUH) to Tokyo (NRT).

In each case, these tickets would typically cost many thousands of dollars, so you’re getting incredible value. When there is award availability, AAdvantage really is a program that’s tough to beat.

Also keep in mind that credit card spending will qualify for Loyalty Points (helping you earn elite status, including Gold, Platinum, Platinum Pro, or Executive Platinum), though the welcome bonus as such won’t. Upon completing minimum spending, you’d earn a minimum of 5,000 Loyalty Points. As I’ll explain below, you can even double dip the Loyalty Points you earn.

The Citi AAdvantage Business Card 75,000-point offer is the best publicly available sign-up bonus that we’ve seen on the card. How do the previous Citi AAdvantage Business Card bonuses compare?

As you can see, the Citi AAdvantage Business Card publicly available welcome offer has most commonly varied from 65,000 to 75,000 miles, so you might as well apply when the offer is the best.

If you’re interested in applying for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, the typical Citi credit card application restrictions apply, including that you can be approved for at most one Citi card every eight days, and at most two Citi cards every 65 days.

On top of that, the bonus isn’t available to those who have received a new account bonus on this exact card in the past 48 months. Eligibility is unrelated to having any other American Airlines credit cards.

There’s not a published credit score you need to get approved for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. Ideally I’d hope to have a credit score of 700+, but people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been denied.

If you’re concerned about Chase’s 5/24 rule, note that applying for a Citi business card generally won’t count toward that limit. I should also mention that at least anecdotally, this card seems to be quite easy to get approved for.

The Citi AAdvantage Business Card has an annual fee that’s waived for the first year, so you can “try” the card before you have to pay a fee. While the fee after that is technically still $99, it’s increasing to $150 as of January 24, 2027, so that’s what you’d pay on account renewal. There’s no cost to add employee cards for authorized users.

With the annual fee increasing as of January 2027, the card will also pick up several valuable new perks, including the following:

This is also my favorite card for earning AAdvantage elite status, since you can essentially earn Loyalty Points for two members at once. Authorized user spending earns Loyalty Points for the authorized user’s AAdvantage account, and also for the primary cardmember’s AAdvantage account.

#6022. Allegiant Air Cancels 17 Routes From 3 Busiest Airports: See Full List Now

Journalist – Aaron is an aviation and travel journalist with 14 years of experience in the travel and tourism industry. His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America. Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand. His work has been published in Simple Flying and featured by MSN, SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel, EIN News, Pakistan Defence, and Climate Depot.

America's ultra-low-cost carrier Allegiant Air has cut 17 routes from its three busiest airports between 2025 and 2026. This comes as the airline continues to reevaluate underperforming routes and redeploy its fleet of Airbus and Boeing narrowbody aircraft elsewhere.

Allegiant, based in Nevada, is a budget airline that operates more than 120 Airbus A319 and A320 family and Boeing 737 MAX 8-200 aircraft. As expected with a no-frills carrier, airfares are usually relatively cheap, but additional fees are incurred for services including checked baggage, seat selection, and meals onboard.

Orlando Sanford, St. Pete-Clearwater, and Punta Gorda are Allegiant's top three airports; combined, they catered for more than 2,299 total departures in November alone. Given Allegiant's business model, it attracts primarily leisure-focused travelers, which is why its domestic-only network serves a large network of destinations in Florida.

At the beginning of 2025, Allegiant decided to end a number of underperforming routes. Data from Cirium, an online aviation analytics company, showed that in March, two routes were terminated; in April, five services were shelved; and in May, a single service to Greensboro was taken offline.

St. Pete–Clearwater International Airport (PIE)

McAllen Miller International Airport (MFE)

St. Pete–Clearwater International Airport (PIE)

Minneapolis–St. Paul International Airport (MSP)

Savannah/Hilton Head International Airport (SAV)

St. Pete–Clearwater International Airport (PIE)

Orlando Sanford International Airport (SFB)

Orlando Sanford International Airport (SFB)

Piedmont Triad International Airport (GSO)

These changes cut specific routes to destinations in Texas, Georgia, Minnesota, Virginia, North Dakota, and North Carolina.

In August 2025, Allegiant undertook another network restructuring, exiting a number of high-cost, underperforming routes. This saw the limited aircraft in its fleet being reassigned to other, more profitable leisure corridors. This included the airline's complete withdrawal from Norfolk.

Its decision to back out of Norfolk came as the airline cited rising per-passenger airport fees, which fundamentally affect how a budget airline operates. Allegiant's withdrawal from Norfolk was also influenced by the rapid expansion of competitors Breeze Airways and Southwest Airlines.

St. Pete–Clearwater International Airport (PIE)

Orlando Sanford International Airport (SFB)

Allegiant removed its Huntington service because it was hyper-seasonal and, following persistent fleet constraints, the airline trimmed routes that could not meet strict profit and load factor targets.

Allegiant has dropped 20 Florida routes, but surprising passenger data reveals many were performing better than expected before cancellation.

This year, Allegiant has shelved six routes as the airline looks to expand operations elsewhere (such as Fort Lauderdale). This restructuring was intended to free up aircraft so the airline could boost its services in Fort Lauderdale by 33%.

As a result, low load factors led to a number of market exits between April and May, with Columbia being dropped just one year after it was launched. New Orleans also had shocking load factorsof around 44%, according to Aviation Shop, prompting the airline to withdraw from the route after just six months of service. A full list of 2026 Florida routes that were terminated includes:

Orlando Sanford International Airport (SFB)

Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY)

St. Pete–Clearwater International Airport (PIE)

St. Pete–Clearwater International Airport (PIE)

Orlando Sanford International Airport (SFB)

Austin–Bergstrom International Airport (AUS)

Orlando Sanford International Airport (SFB)

Overall, these cuts reflect the two-part strategy Allegiant continues to pursue: trimming routes with weak load factors in the spring and pulling aircraft from lower-fare markets to redeploy to high-yielding expansion opportunities.

#6021. Jeffries puts immigration bill high on Democratic priority list

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., holds a news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is signaling Democrats will move quickly on immigration legislation when the party reclaims the House in January, while acknowledging it still has work to do in shaping its healthcare agenda.

Jeffries, who is expected to secure his spot as the next speaker during a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday, identified immigration and health care as among the top priorities for the incoming majority during a Tuesday news conference.

“One of the things that we need to do is to move the Dream and Promise Act for DACA recipients and TPS recipients,” Jeffries said, referring to a Democratic bill introduced last year. “We should actually move that bill immediately.”

The proposal aims to create a path to citizenship for certain Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipients and Temporary Protected Status holders. Similar legislation has been a top priority for Democrats in both chambers for more than a decade, with Democrats unable to advance this bill in the House while Republicans have held the majority.

Jeffries also reiterated his calls to rein in Immigration and Customs Enforcement and redirect funding allocated to the agency through Republicans' budget law known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, while expressing a desire for bipartisan cooperation on immigration more broadly.

“We think the border should be safe and strong and secure, and we think our immigration system overall is broken,” Jeffries said. “We need to fix it in a comprehensive way, and certainly, it's our hope that a handful of Republicans will be willing to join us, so we can fix it in a bipartisan way.”

On healthcare, however, Jeffries offered fewer specifics, suggesting Democrats still have decisions to make before taking control of the chamber. Democrats broadly agree on the need to restore subsidies for plans purchased through health insurance markets that expired at the end of 2025. But the question of what additional steps the party should pursue with the goal of expanding coverage and lowering prices is likely to be a major test of Democratic leadership’s ability to find consensus among its robust new majority.

When asked how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that's all part of an ongoing conversation.”

The New York Democrat outlined several broader healthcare priorities, including reversing Medicaid cuts enacted under President Donald Trump, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits, all of which Democrats have vowed to do over the last year.

“Out of the gate, what we clearly have to do is fix our broken healthcare system in terms of the damage that's been done by Donald Trump and MAGA extremists over the last two years, and that clearly involves reversing the Medicaid cuts and extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits, and beginning to engage in supporting medical research, particularly things like research for pediatric cancer,” Jeffries added.

Democrats established a healthcare working group earlier this Congress, led by Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y. and Terri Sewell, D-Ala., to gather perspectives and develop policy proposals as the party works toward a broader agenda.

Without an announced challenger, Jeffries has expressed confidence that he’ll secure the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who have said they remain “undecided” ahead of Wednesday’s elections. Jeffries, who was introduced as “Speaker Jeffries” on election night, said last week he was “very confident we’ll get there” and confirmed that the caucus will hold a recorded vote in the contest.

Rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to go forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives, many aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America, had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

Jeffries said Tuesday the approach mirrors the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who is best positioned to lead based on “track record, experience and vision.”

This report was corrected to reflect Rep. Nancy Pelosi’s status as a current member.

Booking a table can be the least exciting part of a night out. However, the platform you use to do it can now earn you rewards worth anything from a few cents to a delicious discount on your bill.

OpenTable, DoorDash, Seated and now Resy all reward you for dining out, though each takes a different approach. OpenTable awards its own points, DoorDash issues credits for future orders, Seated offers rewards that can be redeemed for gift cards and Resy awards American Express Membership Rewards points.

As with your favorite coffee chain's loyalty program or a food delivery app subscription, the best option depends on where, how often and how much you eat out. Whichever you choose, you'll generally still earn rewards on eligible restaurant purchases when paying with a dining credit card, making your meal even sweeter.

In this guide, we compare what each program earns, what those rewards are worth and the fine print to watch so you can decide which one deserves a seat at your table.

*Based on TPG's November 2026 valuations.

Related: This overlooked dining program is one of the most generous and gets you $25 off your very first meal

OpenTable Regulars is free to join, and you'll earn 100 dining points for each reservation you book directly on OpenTable while signed in to your account and then complete. Reservations made through restaurant websites or third-party booking partners generally don't qualify. Points are posted only after you've dined, so canceled reservations and no-shows earn nothing.

Some restaurants in the program also offer bonus-point reservations worth 500, 750 or even 1,000 points at certain times. To find them, turn on the "bonus points filter" under special features in the OpenTable app.

Once you have at least 1,000 points, you can redeem them in the app's "Rewards" section at the following rates for U.S. members:

As for the redemption rate you'll get for each, they're:

That means a standard 100-point reservation is only worth 80 cents toward a future meal, and you'll need 20 of them to earn a $16 dining credit, which isn't very rewarding.

Dining credits work at participating OpenTable restaurants (look for the "Dining Credit Accepted" filter). After you redeem your points, you can add the credit to a reservation, which provides a digital Mastercard you can use toward eligible bills. Experience credits work similarly but only apply to certain prepaid experiences, such as prix-fixe menus and cocktail classes. Dining credits expire 12 months after you redeem them.

If you complete six reservations on OpenTable within 12 months, you'll then unlock Gold status for a year. Gold members get priority notifications when tables open up, a three-month complimentary Uber One trial for eligible new or returning members who do not have an active subscription and access to "Gold Tables," which promises harder-to-book tables at more than 500 participating restaurants in over 50 U.S. cities.

OpenTable also partners with Chase, Uber and Visa. Uber One members can book Uber One Exclusive Tables, eligible Visa cardholders can access tables and special events through the Visa Dining Collection and select Chase cardholders get exclusive tables and statement credits (more on that below).

Make sure you're actually turning up for your bookings, though. OpenTable will close your Regulars account and cancel all your points if you record four no-shows within 12 months. Your points also expire after 12 months of inactivity or after 3 years from the date you earn them, whichever comes first.

Related: Earn even more rewards when dining out with OpenTable

DoorDash is best known for delivery, but reservations are now available in select cities across the U.S., Australia and Canada. Its current market page lists 17 U.S. cities, plus Melbourne and Sydney in Australia and Toronto and Vancouver in Canada.

Rather than earn points, you earn promotional DoorDash credits when you book and complete an eligible reservation in the DoorDash app or on its website. The amount is shown before you book and now varies by restaurant, reservation time and membership status. Current U.S. listings commonly advertise $5 in credits, while some times display $10 or $12. Not every reservation earns a credit.

Credits are posted after you've paid for your meal and can be used toward eligible future DoorDash delivery or pickup orders. They typically can't be used to pay for taxes, fees or tips, expire six months after they're issued unless the offer says otherwise, have no cash value and can't be used to buy gift cards or alcohol.

Since the reward is a fixed amount, you don't earn more rewards for a higher food bill. A $5 credit is a 5% return on a $100 dinner but about 1.7% on a $300 tasting menu. A $10 credit would deliver returns of 10% and about 3.3%, respectively. That makes DoorDash Reservations especially appealing for smaller restaurant bills if you already use DoorDash.

DashPass members can earn more on eligible reservations, plus access exclusive prime-time tables and discounts on Lyft Black rides. However, the elevated reservation reward is no longer a simple fixed $2 boost across every listing, so check the offer shown before booking rather than assuming your membership guarantees a particular amount.

Check the restaurant's cancellation policy when you book. Late cancellations and no-shows may incur fees set by the restaurant, and DoorDash says excessive no-shows can result in suspension of your access to reservations.

Outside its reservation cities, DoorDash's "Going Out" tab also lists in-store offers at certain restaurants, with DashPass members earning extra rewards for repeat visits in some locations.

Related: Your complete guide to Chase and DoorDash

What is unique about this program is that you don't need to book through Seated: You link an eligible credit or debit card, then tap to activate the restaurants where you want to earn a higher reward rate before paying with your linked card. Eligible rewards then post automatically, with no receipts to upload.

Activations last until the end of the calendar month, and you can activate up to 25 restaurants per month (plus any monthly specials). Seated's app also advertises 5% back at participating restaurants, even without an activation, provided you open the app at least once every 30 days. Higher reward rates generally require activation, so it's worth activating your favorites at the start of each month and checking the offer terms in the app.

Rewards vary by restaurant but can be up to a generous 35% back, with the rate shown on each restaurant's page before you choose to activate it. Rewards are calculated on your eligible food-and-beverage total before tax and tip, so a restaurant offering 10% back would earn you $10 in Seated rewards on a $100 meal. Since each diner earns on the share they pay with their own linked card, splitting the bill doesn't cost anyone their individual rewards.

Seated partners with more than 2,500 restaurants in certain U.S. markets. Availability varies by city and neighborhood, so check the app for participating locations and current rewards before dining, rather than relying on a fixed city list.

You can then redeem Seated rewards for gift cards in the app's store tab, with available brands to choose from including Airbnb, Amazon, Dunkin', Nordstrom, Sephora, Starbucks, Target and Uber. Because rewards can then be converted to eligible gift cards at face value, TPG values them at $1 per $1 redeemed, provided you choose a brand you'd spend with anyway and meet any minimum redemption requirement.

The catch is that Seated rewards may expire after more than 30 days without qualifying account activity, so check the app's activity and expiration rules rather than assuming opening it alone preserves your balance. Seated also says its rewards can't be combined with other restaurant promotions, third-party deals (such as those available through Groupon) or discount offers.

If you're a new member, keep an eye out for a first-meal bonus offer of up to $10 through an eligible referral link or promotional offer, though this is not guaranteed for every member.

Related: Rove adds dining and in-store rewards in major platform expansion

Resy Rewards takes a different approach than the other three programs. It does not issue a stand-alone Resy currency. Instead, eligible U.S. American Express cardmembers earn 4 additional Membership Rewards points per dollar spent at participating restaurants, on top of the points their enrolled card already earns.

To participate, you must first enroll an eligible U.S. Amex card that earns Membership Rewards points in the Rewards tab of the Resy iOS app.

You must then book a participating restaurant through the Rewards tab, complete the meal and pay with the enrolled card. Merely dining at a participating restaurant or booking it through another part of Resy will not trigger the 4 bonus points per dollar. At launch, the program is only available through the Resy iOS app, meaning Android users cannot currently use it.

The initial New York City list includes restaurants like Carne Mare, Le Crocodile, Hearth, Kiko, Opto and Le Pavillon. American Express plans to expand Resy Rewards to additional U.S. cities and select Tock venues in 2027.

On a $100 eligible restaurant purchase, Resy Rewards would provide 400 bonus Membership Rewards points. Based on our valuation of 2 cents per Membership Rewards point, that is an estimated $8 in value (or an 8% return) before accounting for the card's standard earning rate.

Related: Don't overlook Resy: How to maximize dining experiences and save money with this Amex benefit

Because OpenTable and DoorDash reward reservations with a fixed amount while Seated pays a percentage of your bill and Resy pays a fixed number of points per dollar spent, the best option depends on how much you spend. Here's a comparison for $100 in food-and-drink purchases (before tax and tip), assuming the advertised offers apply and you can use the full value of the DoorDash credits on a later order:

If you spend $200 on a meal rather than $100, the OpenTable and DoorDash rewards stay the same, while the Seated rewards as a percentage of spending will quickly increase. Resy would also double to 800 bonus points, worth an estimated $16 with TPG's valuation of Amex points.

Seated can be the most rewarding option for larger restaurant bills, especially at restaurants that offer higher reward rates. However, its value depends on the percentage offered. DoorDash's fixed credits may still provide you with a better return on smaller bills or at restaurants that offer lower Seated rewards. Resy provides a consistent 8% estimated return from its bonus points — but only at its small number of participating restaurants at launch.

Related: The dining statement credits that save me over $1,000 every year

Certain restaurant purchases can also earn credit card rewards in addition to the benefits provided by these platforms. Combining these apps with a card that earns bonus points at restaurants can be an easy way to double-dip and earn more rewards. Some of the best options currently available include:

But it gets even better. Savvy diners keen on maximizing their rewards may be able to triple-dip by booking an eligible Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables restaurant through OpenTable and paying with their Sapphire Reserve card. Doing so will allow you to earn OpenTable Regulars points plus 3 Chase Ultimate Rewards points per dollar spent on the eligible dining purchase, even if you later receive a statement credit. Qualifying purchases at participating restaurants can also trigger the separate Sapphire Reserve dining credit, worth up to $150 per half-year.

Related: How to double-, triple- or even quadruple-dip on dining rewards

Resy Rewards offers a strong, straightforward points return at participating restaurants. However, the program is launching at only a handful of New York City restaurants and is available through the Resy iOS app, so most diners will not be able to use it regularly yet.

Seated has the highest potential return for larger dining bills. A restaurant offering 15% back would earn you $30 in rewards redeemable for gift cards on a $200 dinner, while a 35% offer would earn $70. Know, though, that higher rates generally require monthly activation, and you'll need to keep your rewards account active.

DoorDash Reservations can still be the best option for smaller meals when the booking carries a strong credit. A $10 or $12 reward can beat percentage-based programs on a modest check. The catch is that rewards now vary by reservation, availability is limited to select cities and the credits are less useful if you rarely order through DoorDash.

OpenTable Regulars is the least rewarding of the four for most standard reservations, with a 100-point booking worth just 80 cents at the best U.S. redemption rate. Still, it is the most broadly available of the four in the markets where its Dining Points program operates and offers useful extras, including bonus-point tables, Gold Tables and a three-month Uber One trial for eligible Gold members. Select Chase cardholders can also receive statement credits at eligible restaurants.

There's no single best dining rewards platform for everyone, as the right choice depends on where you live, how much you spend and how often you dine out.

Resy offers a compelling points return at participating venues, but its limited launch footprint and lack of an Android app make it more of a promising option than an everyday solution right now.

Seated can deliver the biggest reward on an expensive meal, while DoorDash can be particularly rewarding on a smaller bill when the booking offers a decent credit.

As for OpenTable, it remains the most broadly available of the four in the markets where its Dining Points program operates. Its nationwide coverage, Gold perks and Chase partnership make it worth considering, especially when you travel.

Since all four cost nothing to join, you may as well sign up for them all so you are ready the next time you want to book a meal. Just remember to show up for reservations or cancel within the restaurant's deadline, as no-shows can cost you points, credits or even access.

That's some food for thought before your next night out.

#6018. The World's 6 Largest Airbus A321neo Operators In 2026

The single-aisle market has experienced a profound change over the past decade, with extended-range narrowbody aircraft replacing widebodies on transcontinental and regional trunk routes. At the vanguard of this revolution is the ever-popular Airbus A321neo, an airframe that combines unmatched fuel efficiency with transoceanic legs reaching up to 4,000 nautical miles (7,408 kilometers).

At almost any major airport in the world, the A321neo can be found, and that is for good reason. Across the globe, mega-carriers and ultra-low-cost airlines alike have restructured their operational strategies around this versatile jet, but which airlines have built the largest fleets of this aircraft?

This list will showcase the world's six largest operators of the A321neo, focusing on how distinct commercial models use the jet to redefine modern passenger aviation. These range from European ultra-low-cost expansion to Asian mega-growth and American domestic hub dominance.

United Airlines has emerged as a powerhouse operator of the A321neo, expanding its fleet to 80 active aircraft, per Planespotters.net, while maintaining a substantial order book of over 135 additional frames. As part of its aggressive United Next fleet modernization strategy, the carrier has leaned heavily on the A321neo to increase capacity availability on high-density domestic trunk routes and gradually replace aging narrowbody types.

Operating primarily out of its major hubs at Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD), Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), and Denver International Airport (DEN), the type connects high-traffic business and leisure markets that are vital to United's overall network. Passenger experience on United's A321neo fleet centers around a modern three-class cabin layout seating 200 passengers.

The aircraft features 20 domestic first-class recliners at the front, alongside spacious economy seating equipped with the carrier's latest NEXT interior standards. Travelers benefit from high-resolution seatback entertainment touchscreens, Bluetooth audio connectivity for wireless headphones, and significantly larger overhead bins designed to accommodate standard roller bags on their side.

The A321neo is incredibly important for United and its future roadmap. The aircraft provides the range and payload flexibility required to service demanding transcontinental corridors between the East and West coasts. Now operating these modern narrowbodies alongside incoming A321XLRs, United has successfully optimized its single-aisle network to match the capacity and comfort expectations of modern frequent flyers.

A uniquely liveried Coastliner featuring 20 lie-flat Polaris suites and massive seatback screens readies for transcontinental service.

With a growing presence among global leaders, American Airlines operates 96 standard A321neo aircraft, backed by a robust backlog of 127 additional jets on order alongside its separate A321XLR fleet. As highlighted in recent fleet coverage by Simple Flying, these narrowbody aircraft serve as the leader for high-density domestic corridors.

They connect major hubs like Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW), Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT), and Miami International Airport (MIA). Cabin layout choices emphasize a dual-class commercial strategy tailored for domestic business and leisure travelers. American Airlines equips its standard A321neos with a 196-seat configuration.

This layout features 20 domestic first-class recliners at the front, alongside spacious main cabin extra options providing extra legroom of up to 34 inches (86 cm). Passengers benefit from modern amenities including high-speed Wi-Fi, seatback power ports, and personal device entertainment streaming, providing consistent comfort across medium-haul domestic sectors.

Strategically, the introduction of these advanced narrowbodies has allowed American Airlines to retire aging mainline types and therefore optimize seat capacity on high-demand transcontinental and Caribbean routes. The aircraft deliver significant fuel burn reductions compared to older legacy jets. This fleet integration positions the carrier to seamlessly link standard domestic operations with premium-heavy long-haul missions flown by its sister A321XLR fleet.

As the largest carrier in Asia by overall fleet volume, China Southern Airlines is the preeminent Chinese operator of the A321neo. China Southern has 100 active A321neo frames in service, forming an integral pillar of the airline's domestic and regional trunk infrastructure.

Operating mainly out of its mega-hubs at Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport (CAN) and Beijing Daxing International Airport (PKX), the airline deploys these efficient narrowbodies to connect high-density commercial centers across mainland China. It also ventures into key Southeast Asian markets such as Bangkok and Jakarta. China Southern's A321neo fleet cabins reflect a tailored approach to regional comfort.

On this front, it frequently uses a balanced three-class or high-density two-class layout. Standard configurations often seat approximately 195 passengers, incorporating a dedicated premium cabin section featuring four business class recliners, 24 economy comfort seats with expanded legroom, and 167 main cabin seats.

The thoughtful partitioning allows the carrier to capture high-yielding domestic business travelers as well as servicing high-volume leisure demand on trunk sectors. The integration of the A321neo has allowed China Southern to greatly improve route economics amidst intense domestic competition.

What makes the A321neo so invaluable for China Southern is its ability to seamlessly handle multi-hour domestic and regional legs spanning up to 3,500 nautical miles (6,482 kilometers), encompassing the entirety of the major population centers in China. Ultimately, China Southern has bolstered its major hub operations with versatile narrowbody capacity, producing the operational flexibility needed to manage China's sprawling aviation network.

The largest A321neo operator in North America is Delta Air Lines, which operates a robust fleet approaching 111 active aircraft supported by nearly 90 firm future orders. As a cornerstone of Delta's long-term narrowbody renewal program, the A321neo operates high-density domestic trunk routes.

It connects major hubs like Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport (MSP), and Boston Logan International Airport (BOS). Delta's A321neo fleet is notable for its innovative cabin configurations, including a premium-heavy subfleet layout tailored for high-yielding markets.

While standard layouts feature 20 first-class recliners, 60 Comfort+ extra-legroom seats, and 114 main cabin seats, newly updated configurations incorporate an expansive 44-seat Delta First cabin. This high-premium arrangement dedicates roughly 60% of the aircraft to premium seating, meeting robust corporate demand as well as satisfying exceptional passenger load factors across competitive domestic routes.

Passenger comfort across the fleet is enhanced by comprehensive modern amenities, including seatback entertainment screens, in-seat power outlets, and high-speed in-flight connectivity. Powered by Pratt & Whitney GTF engines, the aircraft combines industry-leading fuel efficiency with a quiet, spacious cabin environment. Delta has positioned its A321neo fleet as a benchmark for premium narrowbody operations in modern commercial aviation.

India's largest airline, IndiGo, comes in at a close second globally in A321neo operations, with fleet counts hovering around 181 aircraft in service. Operating in one of the world's fastest-growing aviation markets, the carrier has turned to the narrowbody's efficiency to connect high-density domestic city pairs across the Indian subcontinent.

Simultaneously, it has extended its international reach into the Middle East, Southeast Asia, and Central Asia. IndiGo's relentless domestic expansion has been in part due to its high aircraft utilization rates, often turning planes around in under 30 minutes at busy hubs. What truly distinguishes IndiGo's position in the global A321neo landscape is its monumental order book.

The airline has hundreds of additional A321neos and long-range A321XLRs slated for delivery over the coming decade, pushing its ultimate commitment toward more than 600 aircraft of the type. As such, IndiGo is widely projected to surpass Wizz Air as the world's absolute largest operator of the airframe, as noted by The Hindu.

The massive influx of narrowbody capacity is fundamental to the airline's long-term growth strategy, allowing it to up-gauge high-demand trunk routes and significantly lower operating costs per available seat-mile. To support its high-frequency regional network, IndiGo equips its A321neos in dense single-class configurations optimized for maximum passenger capacity and operational turnaround speed.

Topping the global leaderboards as the largest operator of the A321neo is Wizz Air, the Hungarian ultra-low-cost carrier that has staked its entire aggressive expansion strategy on the type. Wizz Air has 185 active A321neo frames in service across its operating subsidiaries, including Wizz Air Hungary, Wizz Air Malta, and Wizz Air UK.

It is supported by a colossal backlog designed to phase out older ceo variants. Operating from key bases across Central and Eastern Europe, the airline uses the aircraft's exceptional fuel economy to open many point-to-point leisure routes spanning across Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa.

Wizz Air configures its high-density A321neos in a single-class layout accommodating 239 passengers, per Seat Maps, which is designed to maximize seat-mile cost efficiency. The ultra-dense seating arrangement features a functional pitch of approximately 28 to 29 inches (71 to 74 cm) alongside 18-inch (46 cm) wide seats.

This enables the carrier to offer highly competitive fares while maintaining strong profitability on high-density sun and city-break corridors. Like many other ultra-low-cost airlines, Wizz Air has standardized its cockpit and cabin operations around the A321neo, and in doing so, has cemented its status as the premier European champion of Airbus narrowbody technology.

Furthermore, the carrier is actively modernizing its onboard product to enhance passenger comfort in a way that does not sacrifice unit economics. Wizz Air has introduced updated lightweight seating partnerships with manufacturer Geven, alongside modern LED ambient lighting and advanced cabin features across incoming deliveries.
